# Microsoft Graph app management policies and adding a certificate: a pinned copy of Learn's samples

This folder is an unmodified copy of four Microsoft Learn source pages: [Update tenantAppManagementPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/tenantappmanagementpolicy-update?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Create appManagementPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/appmanagementpolicy-post?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Assign appliesTo](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/appmanagementpolicy-post-appliesto?view=graph-rest-1.0) and [Add a certificate to an app by using Microsoft Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/applications-how-to-add-certificate). They hold Microsoft's v1.0 HTTP samples for the tenant default app management policy, an app-specific policy and its assignment, and the PATCH of an application's `keyCredentials` that adds a certificate. They come from [microsoftgraph/microsoft-graph-docs-contrib](https://github.com/microsoftgraph/microsoft-graph-docs-contrib/tree/bb35043c742d4406d73ccae904c05fbfca7c7428) at commit `bb35043c742d4406d73ccae904c05fbfca7c7428`, retrieved October 30, 2026. The repository's code license (`LICENSE-CODE`) is MIT; its documentation license (`LICENSE`) is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.

**Why the pages, not just the samples.** The HTTP samples exist only inside these pages; the SDK snippets they include are generated from them. Pinning the pages byte for byte keeps the copy checkable against upstream. `examples/non-person-identity/tests/CredentialPolicySampleHarness.ps1` parses the HTTP samples, unmodified, at test time and sends them to Chapter 04's fake Microsoft Graph. Nothing is installed and nothing signs in. The [developer workbook *Building Non-Person Identity*, Chapter 04](../../../docs/project-plans/developer-workbooks/non-person-identity/04-app-management-policies-and-certificate-rotation.md) links Learn rather than quoting the pages.

**How it stays honest.**

- `snapshot.json` records the upstream repository, paths, commit, dates, licenses and the size and SHA-256 of every file here. Each file's git blob hash was checked against the upstream tree at that commit before the manifest was written. `scripts/tests/test_third_party_snapshots.py` fails if any file is changed, added or removed.
- The weekly source watch follows commits to each upstream page (`graph-tenant-app-policy-update-commits`, `graph-app-policy-create-commits`, `graph-app-policy-assign-commits` and `graph-add-certificate-howto-commits` in `data/source-watch/feeds.json`) and reports each one in its issue under DW (developer workbooks).
- To move to a newer upstream commit: review the upstream change, copy the pages from that commit, regenerate `snapshot.json`, rerun `examples/non-person-identity/tests/NpiCredentialPolicy.Tests.ps1` and the Chapter 04 labs, and open a pull request. Never edit the files here; changes the program needs go in `examples/non-person-identity`.

These files keep their upstream bytes, line endings included, so the hashes match the upstream commit.
